newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe stocks mixed to weak on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe stocks mixed to weak on profit-taking.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrial shares were mixed to weak on profit-taking in an active market on Wednesday.

The key industrial index slid 116.75 points -- or 1.4 percent -- to end at 7,970.19, dragged down mainly by cigarette manufacturer Rothmans' 200-cent drop to 3,600 and horticulture company Ariston's 50-cent loss to 1,550.
"There's a bit of profit-taking because some of the counters were overpriced so we're going to see them coming off," one dealer said.
"But the market is really mixed. There're a lot of buyers out there with lots of foreign trading."

Also among the day's losers, hotel group Zimsun, sugar refinery ZSR, finance houses UDC and Finhold all shed 10 cents to 400, 1,390, 240 and 990 respectively while local conglomerate TA Holdings at 165, seed manufacturer and distributor Seedco at 190, textiler David Whitehead at 65 all eased five cents.

Stocks to gain included publishing group Zimpapers which rose 50 cents to 2,100, pork processor Colcom which gained 30 cents to 370, engineering company Gulliver which climbed 20 cents to 190. Farm implements-maker Zimplow and discount house DCZ both added 10 cents to 360 and 180 respectively.
In minings, gold producer Rio Tinto at 3,500 and Wankie Colliery at 365 both traded unchanged while copper mine Mhangura added 10 cents to 40.
However, gold producer Ashanti slid 300 cents to 13,500 and the mining index slipped a marginal 0.19 points to 1,236.77.
